title: Etale/pro-etale comparison respects the canonical open tensor map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work on small representatives of the ordinary etale and pro-etale sites in a common larger universe, with the unbounded derived categories of constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact derived comparison pullback [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Let $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $N\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ be arbitrary. Write
$$e_F:A_Xj^{e}_!F\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{p}_!A_UF$$
for the degreewise derived comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], using exact extensions by zero [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Superscripts $e,p$ distinguish the two sites. Let $t_T:A_T(F\otimes^L G)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_TF\otimes^L A_TG$ be the canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and let $a_j:A_Uj_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_p^*A_X$ be the canonical derived pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Define
$$h_{K,N}=(1\otimes a_{j,N})\circ t_U:
 A_U(K\otimes^Lj_e^*N)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_UK\otimes^Lj_p^*A_XN.$$
Let $\gamma^e_{K,N}:j^e_!K\otimes^LN\xrightarrow{\sim}j^e_!(K\otimes^Lj_e^*N)$ and $\gamma^p_{A_UK,A_XN}$ be the canonical open tensor comparisons of [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor, lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. Then the following equality holds in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, naturally in $K,N$:
$$
j^p_!(h_{K,N})\circ e_{K\otimes^Lj_e^*N}\circ A_X(\gamma^e_{K,N})
=\gamma^p_{A_UK,A_XN}\circ(e_K\otimes1)\circ t_X,
$$
as maps from $A_X(j^e_!K\otimes^LN)$ to $j^p_!(A_UK\otimes^Lj_p^*A_XN)$. No boundedness, constructibility, properness, or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Use the recorded exact comparison and exact extensions by zero, and their canonical localized comparison e. Compute the mate of the literal open-restriction comparison: on sections it is the usual direct-image comparison. Transport from literal restriction to the chosen pullback using the canonical adjunction isomorphisms. Applying the mates correspondence twice identifies the inverse extension comparison with the support-site pullback comparison. The unit equation then descends to the unbounded derived categories by CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mapDerivedCategoryAdjunction_mate.

Use the canonical tensorators and the existing source-library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.comparisonCompatible_leftDerivedComparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso. Transport the comparison functors from their total left derived presentations to their exact termwise derived presentations. Expand the canonical composition isomorphisms to identify the resulting square with a_j inverse. Invert the pullback tensorators and transport their first argument along Lj^* = Dj^*. Naturality and the inverse identities give precisely the compatibility with the mixed tensorators that define the two open projection maps.

Apply the generic projection-map mate theorem to the derived open adjunctions, the extension comparison inverse, the localized restriction square and the tensorators. Its unit hypothesis is step 1 and its tensor hypothesis is step 2. The site-specific projection maps are, by definition, the maps attached to these exact adjunctions and mixed tensorators, so no independent normalization theorem is required.

Precompose the resulting equation with the inverse of the etale projection map and the extension comparison, and postcompose with the inverse pro-etale projection map. Cancel inverse pairs, including the tensor of the extension comparison. Functoriality identifies the two remaining maps inside j_! with h=(1 tensor a_j) composed with t_U. This is the claimed equality, for arbitrary unbounded K and N. All comparisons used are natural in both inputs.
